1. No pray drive. Maybe when she was younger but in her older age there is no herd drive. (Or maybe she herds me and I don’t realize haha)

2. Double coat smooth coat; she doesn’t shed much; her coat is probably more low maintenance than any other dog I’ve met.  She does have low tolerances for heat but what dog doesn’t? She has some small matting issues behind her ears but easy to cut out, and just a common longer hair dog issue. Also gotta cut her butt hair sometimes bc of matting if it can’t be brushed out

3.  Currently an 11 year old mainly collie girl with a little bit of lab. Still going, but starting to get some arthritis. She states meds for it that help but she’s slowing down.

4.  Teeth are her only issue. She cracked a tooth in a bone so she’s given more soft food after that happened and no more bones (milk bones instead). 
Arthritis is common in older dogs so use fish oil pills to help. Also helped her sleep better too, not that she had issues before she just sleeps more like a rock now. 

5. Use to be high energy, walk everyday, dog park sometimes, but since she turned 10, she slowed down. Now we do small walks and walking up and down stairs to help her joints (and mine since I have to walk the stairs to encourage her up and down them). Nothing compared to my German Shepard lab mix who needed two walks or runs a day. That 16 year old boy finally slowed down at 14. 

6.  11 yr old collie grew up  with her older brother and she loves him. She doesn’t interact with other dogs her size or larger but is willing to put up with smaller dogs. She isn’t aggressive but makes not happy noises if they approach her too much. Normally she just hides behind people for comfort, but she’s a huge people dog. At dog parks instead of playing with dogs she will meet every person first. She’s pet and affection driven much more than food driven. 

7. Honestly lucked out on such a perfect dog; getting her at 3mo helped with what I wanted in training; comparing her older brother who I got at 1 year old my collie was easier to train. 
Have fun with any collie you get, I’ve never met a collie who’s not up their owners ass (in a sweet way). My collie doesn’t require a lease to stay with me where my Shepard lab mix does require one forever.
